solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 25 hinds: unusually small working animals

indicators.note: unusually says the letters are set out in an unusual new order

parts.note: the answer to 25 across, a horned beast, needed here in the plural to match hinds

explanation.surface: A herd of deer that are, oddly, little beasts of burden.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' must be read as the plural of the 25-across answer: the singular leaves the letter pool one S short.
explanation.definitionFit: These hardy little horses from the Scottish islands were bred to carry peat and work down coal mines.

clue.text: Foul place to see Aunt Sally skipping foxtrot?

indicators.note: skipping means leaving out, so one letter is dropped from the fairground

parts.note: Aunt Sally is a traditional game of throwing sticks at a dummy, a stall found at a funfair
Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A complaint that a trip to the fair to see a fairground game missed out the dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British pub and fairground game where you throw sticks at a dummy's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A foul tackle or foul play is unjust, against the rules, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Bird call drove rook away

parts.note: to call someone on the phone is to ring them

indicators.note: away says the piece is sent off, removed from the word before it

parts.note: R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A bird's cry chased off a crow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' looks like another bird alongside 'Bird', but it is the chess piece, abbreviated R.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the wood pigeon, a common grey European pigeon with white neck patches.

clue.text: Let that decaff brew on the hob for prodigal son

definitions.text: on the hob for prodigal son

indicators.note: to brew is to mix and stew things together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave decaffeinated coffee to stew on the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brew' looks like part of the coffee-making picture, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible parable, the father kills the best-fed young beast to feast on when his wayward son returns home.

clue.text: Brie, red wine frequently left one below par

indicators.note: letters are left out at frequent regular intervals, so every other letter of these words is kept

explanation.surface: Cheese and wine have left someone feeling a bit under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below par' looks like feeling unwell after the cheese and wine, but it is golf.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a hole completed in one stroke fewer than the standard score is this.

clue.text: Patient character's office role?

parts.note: Job, the Bible figure famous for patience, gives a name to which a title is attached: a description of a position held at work

explanation.surface: Asking what post a long-suffering person holds at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' reads as a hospital patient, but it points to Job, the biblical man of patience; his name with a title is a designation in an office.
explanation.definitionFit: Designations like 'manager' or 'clerk' name what someone does at their workplace.

clue.text: Hill outside the fringes of Nuneaton from which men are barred?

indicators.note: outside says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a hill is a height, a raised piece of ground

indicators.note: the fringes are the outermost letters of the word

explanation.surface: A hill just beyond the edges of Nuneaton, a Midlands town, where men are not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barred' hints at a pub bar, apt for a pre-wedding celebration for women only. Nuneaton is a town in Warwickshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's pre-wedding party with her female friends, the British equivalent of a bachelorette party, excludes men.

clue.text: Mother necked miso soup, an item on the bar menu

definitions.text: an item on the bar menu

indicators.note: to neck is to swallow quickly, so the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: Ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: soup suggests something stirred up and mixed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mum gulped down a Japanese broth, ordered from the bar's list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'necked' is British slang for drank quickly, here a container signal; 'soup' looks like part of the miso picture but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This cocktail of sparkling wine and orange juice is a drink you might order at a bar.

clue.text: Fair challenge for one hoping to bring home the bacon?

definitions.text: Fair challenge for one hoping to bring home the bacon?

parts.words: Fair challenge for one hoping to bring home the bacon?
parts.note: at a country fair contestants try to catch a young pig smeared with fat; to bring home the bacon means to win the prize, here literally a pig

explanation.surface: A contest at a fair for someone wanting to earn a living.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'bring home the bacon' is an idiom for earning money or winning, taken literally here.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasing a slippery young pig coated in lard is a traditional fairground contest; the catcher keeps the animal.

clue.text: Terribly nervous son left razor and foam pop sent

indicators.note: left means gone away, so one letter departs from the kit

parts.note: a razor and foam make up a shaving kit

indicators.note: to pop is to burst, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A worried boy has left his shaving things and a fizzy drink has been posted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes S out of SHAVINGKIT; 'pop' rearranges SENT into TENS.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom, chiefly British, for being extremely anxious or agitated, as a cat might be when giving birth.

clue.text: Time to chew over note from guitarist

indicators.note: over says the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: to gnaw is to chew persistently

explanation.surface: A moment to mull over a sound from a guitar player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chew over' looks like a single phrase meaning ponder, but 'over' is the reversal signal on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A plucked string produces a resonant, vibrating sound, especially from a guitar.

clue.text: Criminal German lady pursued by Detective Sergeant Lawrence King

parts.note: Frau is German for a married woman
DS is the abbreviation for a police detective sergeant
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, is known by his initials
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A German woman is chased by a policeman and two famous figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler or cheat who deceives others for gain is a lawbreaker, so the noun fits.

clue.text: Perhaps John Lennon song left on board

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A Beatle's tune was left aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool's Liverpool John Lennon terminal is named after the singer, so he is an example; 'song' looks like part of the Lennon picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool's air terminal is officially named after the former Beatle, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Laziness of Maitre Nicolas in retirement

indicators.note: in retirement says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A French head waiter or lawyer named Nicolas is idle now he has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters AITRENI run across 'Maitre Nicolas' and 'in retirement' turns them round; no separate word signals the hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggishness or a tendency to stay still and do nothing is idleness, the sense of lethargy.

clue.text: HT: Everton on edge, getting hammered — it's unthinkable!

indicators.note: hammered means beaten out of shape, so these letters are bashed into a new order

explanation.surface: At half time, Everton football club are nervous and taking a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: HT is short for half time; Everton is a Liverpool football club. 'getting hammered' looks like the score but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial exclamation telling someone a subject is too awful even to consider or discuss.

clue.text: It's futile turning revolver on a Conservative

indicators.note: turning says the word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a revolver is a type of gun
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: It's pointless pointing a pistol at a right-wing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' could suggest turning by itself, but it is the gun; 'turning' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for something of no value or force, worthless and ineffective.

clue.text: Absent-mindedly played with tweed?

parts.note: fiddling idly with something, such as the cloth of a jacket, is turning it about with the fingers; the cloth name has similar sounds

explanation.surface: Someone fiddled idly with a jacket's woollen cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Tweed is a rough woollen fabric; the clue suggests fidgeting with it while thinking of other things.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidgeting idly with something, turning it round in the fingers, describes the action.

clue.text: Natural gold golf clubs featuring a new iron tip

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Golf clubs of genuine gold, with an iron that has a new tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featuring' says the clubs come with A, N and the iron's tip before them.
explanation.definitionFit: Produce grown without artificial chemicals is described as natural, and the word also means arising from nature.

clue.text: Wind up gramophone component?

definitions.meaning: to wind someone up is to tease or annoy them, to provoke
the stylus of an old record player is a sharp pin that runs in the groove

explanation.surface: Crank the handle of an old record player.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke someone is to goad them, and the stylus of a record player is a thin sharp pointed pin.

clue.text: Getting frosted cake decoration on top

parts.note: icing is the sugary coating used to decorate a cake
up means on top, above

explanation.surface: A cake being covered in a sugar topping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frosted' and 'cake decoration' share the baking picture, but 'frosted' is about freezing weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Windscreens or aircraft wings gaining a layer of ice are becoming coated with frost.

clue.text: Ape/baboon regularly caught in trap

indicators.note: caught in says the following letters are held inside the trap

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: An ape or baboon often gets snared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' is a gin, an old word for an animal snare, not the mouth; 'regularly' takes the odd letters of 'baboon'.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-armed tree-swinging primate of Southeast Asia is one of the lesser apes.

clue.text: Pint he's loth to swallow, here ideally for a drive?

indicators.note: the words swallow the answer, holding it inside them across their breaks

explanation.surface: A drinker reluctant to down a beer before driving.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a position where a golfer's drive or a car's position is ideal; 'drive' points to the pint-and-car picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the ideal spot, ready and positioned perfectly, is the idiom; a drive would be well placed there.

clue.text: Young socialite, upper-class, grand, to scrub drive

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering society
U is the British label for upper-class usage
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A posh young woman with money to burn has to clean the driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' reads as a driveway, but it is a computer's disk drive.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove errors from computer software or hardware is to clean it of faults.

clue.text: Small hotel "run poorly" — sounds harsh!

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
poorly is British for unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A complaint that a little hotel is badly managed comes across as unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run poorly' reads as bad management, but it is R plus ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A piercing, high-pitched voice or noise is grating on the ear.

clue.text: Horny beast, perhaps 21, grabbing poor Elton

indicators.note: grabbing says the first piece takes the second into its grasp

parts.note: the answer to 21 down is an example of an ape

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A randy creature, perhaps a primate, seizes a hapless pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps 21' means the 21-down answer is an example of the piece needed; 'Horny' suggests lust but means having horns.
explanation.definitionFit: This African grazing animal carries horns, so it is a horned creature.
